title: Doc's Sports AI-v3 Review 2026: Pricing, Record, Worth It?
description: Doc's Sports AI-v3 review, checked 7 Nov 2026: the $89 to $595 prices, what the profit since inception claim leaves out, and what we could verify.
dek: An "artificial intelligence" pick feed sold by Doc's Sports, sent by text message for $89 for 3 days, $195 a week or $595 a month. The page claims +23,180 profit since inception. It shows no pick log, does not explain the units, and the product has been renamed from v1 to v2 to v3 while the running total carried on.

status.label: Not verified
status.note: Watchdog has not graded a full, time stamped record of Doc's Sports AI-v3 picks. This page reports what we could check and labels everything else.

short_answer: Doc's Sports AI-v3 is a real product from a long running pick seller. Doc's names an operator and a mailing address, prints the prices, and says picks arrive by text message, 1 to 4 messages a day per service. In that narrow sense it is legitimate.

Whether the model makes money is a different question, and nothing we could open answers it. The page claims "+23,180 Profit Since Inception" and "+18,620" in 2026, but it shows no picks, no odds, no post times and no unit size. Earlier copies of the same page, saved by the Wayback Machine, show the product sold as AI-v1 in 2025 and AI-v2 in June 2026, with the same running total carried forward.
Treat AI-v3 as a seller with marketing totals, not a proven model. If you buy, buy short, log every text yourself with the line and time it arrived, and judge it after a few hundred picks.

guarantee: The AI-v3 page says nothing about a guarantee. The general Doc's terms say: "Once a product or service has been purchased and delivered or viewed, there are no refunds." They add that a guarantee usually means an extension, that one day packages may get a credit, and that "All other services and packages will be reviewed and accounts will be extended at the sole discretion of the staff."

So for a 3 day, weekly or monthly AI-v3 package, the most a losing buyer can expect from the written terms is an extension that staff may or may not grant. We found no cash refund terms and no automatic renewal terms on the pages we opened. Losses on the bets themselves are never covered.

claims_note: The totals are at least consistent with each other. In January 2026 the page claimed +4,560 for 2025, and today's +23,180 since inception minus +18,620 in 2026 also leaves 4,560. That means the "since inception" figure includes results sold under the AI-v1 name in 2025, before AI-v3 existed.

The same seller numbers show a weak stretch the headline hides. On 12 June 2026 the page claimed +15,735 in 2026 and "Zero Losing Months So Far!!" By 7 Nov the 2026 total had grown only 2,885, less than the +3,450 it claims for October alone, so by its own figures the rest of that span, taken together, lost money. The page now counts nine winning months from January through October, which means at least one month from June on did not win.

The page never explains what +23,180 measures. Doc's figures like this usually mean profit for a bettor risking a set dollar amount per unit, but the unit size, the odds taken and the number of picks are not shown.
record: Independently verifiable: nothing we found. We found no time stamped log of every AI-v3 pick held by a third party, no contest run by someone else, and no regulator or court record about results.

Seller's own marketing: running profit totals on the AI-v3 page and the homepage roster, a monthly total for October, and member notes such as "2-0 Monday! +800 (Nov 2)". None of these lists the picks, the odds or the post times, so a buyer cannot rebuild them.

What we can check is the history of the claims. Wayback Machine copies show the page as AI-v1 on 7 Oct 2025 ("70% ALL SPORTS RUN (+4,250)"), still AI-v1 on 18 Jan 2026 ("+5,700 Profit Since Inception"), AI-v2 on 12 Jun 2026 ("+20,295 Profit Since Inception", with "+19,595" further down the same page), and AI-v3 today. The name changed twice; the record behind it was never published.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Doc's Sports AI-v3 is close to nonexistent. We found no review, forum thread or Reddit post that discusses the AI product by name. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: The "Member Notes" box on the AI-v3 page is written by Doc's, not by buyers. It reports the running totals and a recent 2-0 day. It tells you what the seller wants to highlight, not what a typical buyer experienced.

In a TheRX thread about Doc's Sports in general, a member said Doc's handicappers highlight hot runs and hide cold streaks, and that some are worth betting against. The thread does not mention the AI product, he posted no log, and we did not verify his claims.
Web searches of Reddit, TheRX, Covers and SBR for Doc's Sports AI-v3 found no discussion of the product. Trustpilot blocked our check, and there is no app to rate, since picks arrive by text message.

conflicts: The Doc's FAQ says: "We have a list of offshore sports book that we have complete confidence in. We suggest that you give a couple of these a try." A free pick shown on the Doc's SMS terms page on 7 Nov 2026 listed the line as "Offered at: BookMaker". A seller that steers readers to particular sportsbooks may have a financial interest in their betting, whatever the picks do.
Offshore sportsbooks are not licensed by U.S. state regulators. Check the law where you live before you follow that advice.
AI-v3 is a house product of Doc's Sports, sold beside its human handicappers. Doc's both runs the model and publishes the only numbers about it.
strengths: A named operator, a mailing address, a toll free phone line and printed prices.
Short packages exist. A buyer can test it for 3 days at $89 before paying $595 for a month.
The running totals add up across the archived versions, so the seller is at least not rewriting old totals from one copy to the next.
concerns: No public pick log. Every number is a seller total with no picks, odds or unit size.
"Since inception" includes results from earlier versions sold under other names.
By the seller's own figures, the period since mid June outside October lost money, and the June "zero losing months" line no longer holds.
No guarantee is stated for AI-v3, and the site terms rule out refunds once picks are delivered.
The marketing leans on claims nobody can check, such as betting ticket data it says not to ask about.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It is a real product sold by Doc's Enterprises, a long running pick seller with a named address and printed prices. We could not verify that the model wins over time, because Doc's publishes only profit totals and no log of the picks.
How much does Doc's Sports AI-v3 cost?

On 7 Nov 2026 the AI-v3 page listed $89.00 for 3 days, $195.00 for a week and $595.00 for 30 days, with picks sent by text message. The site terms say there are no refunds once picks are delivered, and the page states no guarantee.
Does Doc's Sports AI-v3 have a verified record?

No. The page claims +23,180 since inception and +18,620 in 2026, but shows no picks, odds, post times or unit size, and we found no third party log or audit. The total also carries over results sold under the AI-v1 and AI-v2 names.
Is Doc's Sports AI-v3 worth it?

You get 1 to 4 text messages a day of model picks across sports, at about $20 to $30 a day. What is unproven is the edge itself: the only evidence is the seller's own totals, which by their own numbers include losing stretches since June, and no money comes back if the picks lose.
